prompt:
Extract and normalize the single contact record in the user's note. Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country. Every value must be a JSON string or null. No Markdown or surrounding text.

Select sources before editing values. Use only the record block of Label<sep>value lines; labels can vary and lines can be shuffled. Separators include colon, equals and tab, with optional surrounding spaces. Split at the label separator, preserving punctuation inside the value. Ignore all surrounding notes and signatures. Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Treat absent or empty values and these whole-value placeholders, case-insensitively, as missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD.

Take the country only from the country line, subject to the missing-country exception below. For email and phone, match by content across the record, not by the label: a value with @ supplies email; a value with at least seven digits and no characters other than digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after stripping a leading tel: and a trailing extension supplies phone. Extension forms are ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12 and extension 12, where the digits stand for the extension number. For name and company, use their respective lines unless the name-line value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company-line value does not; in that case swap them before cleaning.

Email: strip surrounding angle brackets and the mailto: prefix wherever it sits relative to the brackets. Lowercase the selected address itself, copying every character apart from casing and the specified wrapper removal. Never repair, regenerate, transliterate or add accents to it based on another field.

Name: split at the first comma if present and move the portion after it before the portion preceding it. Remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx or Prof, with or without a dot, ignoring case. In each space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate.

Company: match and remove a trailing legal suffix case-insensitively, including an optional preceding comma. Use this same list for the swap test: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character of each space-separated word and lowercase the rest. Keep values trimmed and whitespace collapsed.

Country and phone: normalize a supplied country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 from an English, Swedish or German name or an alpha-2 or alpha-3 code, regardless of case. Also recognize UK and Great Britain as GB, Holland as NL, USA and U.S.A. as US, Türkiye as TR, and Czech Republic as CZ.
- After stripping tel: and the extension, test the phone for a leading + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis. If international, replace 00 with +, remove (0), spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and keep the written calling code. If the country is missing, fill it from that code only when the code uniquely identifies a country. Shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. A supplied country stays unchanged by the phone even when they disagree.
- Otherwise the phone is national: strip formatting punctuation and spaces, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the supplied country's calling code. With no record country, return null for a national phone.

The phone format is E.164: + followed only by calling-code and national significant digits. Missing fields are null, never empty strings. The international-phone rule is the only exception to missing values staying null. Do not fill fields from notes, signatures, email domains or company suffixes.
